title: Aaron Journeys to Jerusalem
summary: After Ammon and his brethren separated in the borders of the Lamanite land, Aaron journeys toward Jerusalem, near the borders of Mormon.

explicit_facts.text: Ammon and his brethren separated themselves in the borders of the land of the Lamanites.
Aaron journeyed toward the land called Jerusalem by the Lamanites; it was away joining the borders of Mormon.

unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of the landscape and travelers.
The precise route and distance.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Ammon or Aaron's brethren accompanying Aaron on his journey.

title: Jerusalem and Its People
summary: Lamanites, Amalekites, and the people of Amulon built the great city of Jerusalem. The Amalekites and Amulonites caused the Lamanites to harden their hearts and grow in wickedness.

explicit_facts.text: Lamanites, Amalekites, and the people of Amulon built the great city called Jerusalem.
The Amalekites and Amulonites were harder than the Lamanites and caused them to harden their hearts and wax strong in wickedness and abominations.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The city is established as a great city.
unspecified_visual_details: The city’s architecture, layout, and appearance.
How the people’s hardening of hearts is visually represented.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: The description of hardened hearts and wickedness is not a separate supernatural visual event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a specific act of wickedness not stated in the verses.

title: Aaron Enters a Synagogue
summary: Aaron comes to Jerusalem and begins preaching to the Amalekites in their synagogues, built after the order of the Nehors.

explicit_facts.text: Aaron came to Jerusalem and first began to preach to the Amalekites.
The Amalekites had built synagogues after the order of the Nehors; many Amalekites and Amulonites were after that order.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Aaron preaching inside a synagogue to assembled people.
unspecified_visual_details: The synagogue’s appearance and furnishings.
The people’s clothing and specific arrangement.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse reports the order of the synagogues; it does not describe its visual features.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show Nehor as physically present.

title: An Amalekite Challenges Aaron
summary: Aaron enters a synagogue and speaks to the people. An Amalekite arises and contends with him, questioning his testimony, repentance, and the people's righteousness, worship, and belief that God will save all men.

explicit_facts.text: Aaron entered one of their synagogues to preach to the people and was speaking to them.
An Amalekite arose and began to contend with Aaron.
The Amalekite asked about Aaron's testimony, angels, and whether the people were as good as Aaron's people.
The Amalekite questioned the need for repentance and the judgment of the people's righteousness; he said they had built sanctuaries, assembled to worship God, and believed God would save all men.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The Amalekite stands while addressing Aaron.
unspecified_visual_details: The synagogue's architecture, clothing, expressions, and gestures.

spoken_dialogue.text: How knowest thou that we have cause to repent?
spoken_dialogue.speaker: An Amalekite

spoken_dialogue.text: Behold, we have built sanctuaries, and we do assemble ourselves together to worship God.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: An Amalekite

spoken_dialogue.text: We do believe that God will save all men.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: An Amalekite

narration.text: as Aaron entered into one of their synagogues to preach unto the people
there arose an Amalekite and began to contend with him

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The statements about sanctuaries, worship, and salvation are the Amalekite's claims, not independently narrated facts.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict an angel; the Amalekite only asks about one.
Do not depict the sanctuaries being built or a separate worship gathering.
Do not give Aaron unquoted dialogue.

title: Aaron Questions the Amalekite
summary: Aaron asks whether the man believes the Son of God will come to redeem mankind from their sins. The man rejects Aaron’s knowledge and what he calls foolish traditions.

explicit_facts.text: Aaron asked the man whether he believed the Son of God would come to redeem mankind from their sins.
The man said they did not believe Aaron knew such things, rejected the traditions, and denied knowledge of things to come by Aaron’s fathers or their own.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Aaron and the Amalekite continue their exchange in the synagogue.
unspecified_visual_details: The speakers’ expressions and gestures.

spoken_dialogue.text: Believest thou that the Son of God shall come to redeem mankind from their sins?
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Aaron

spoken_dialogue.text: We do not believe that thou knowest any such thing.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: An Amalekite

spoken_dialogue.text: We do not believe in these foolish traditions.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: An Amalekite

spoken_dialogue.text: We do not believe that thou knowest of things to come,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: An Amalekite

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The man’s words continue through the rest of Alma 21:8; the scene’s spoken text uses only short exact excerpts.

title: Aaron Opens the Scriptures
summary: Aaron opens the scriptures and expounds the coming of Christ, the resurrection, and redemption through Christ’s death, sufferings, and atonement. The people become angry, mock him, and refuse to hear.

explicit_facts.text: Aaron opened the scriptures concerning Christ’s coming, the resurrection of the dead, and redemption through Christ’s death, sufferings, and atonement.
As Aaron expounded these things, the people were angry, mocked him, and would not hear him.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Aaron holding or consulting scriptures while teaching.
unspecified_visual_details: The scriptures’ physical form and appearance.
The specific gestures of the people mocking him.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verses summarize Aaron’s teaching; they do not provide direct quotations of it.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Christ’s coming, resurrection, or atonement as a present visual event.

title: Aaron Leaves for Ani-Anti
summary: Aaron leaves the synagogue and goes to Ani-Anti, where he finds Muloki preaching with Ammah and his brethren; they contend with many about the word.

explicit_facts.text: Aaron departed from the synagogue and came to Ani-Anti.
Aaron found Muloki preaching, along with Ammah and his brethren; they contended with many about the word.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Aaron arriving while Muloki, Ammah, and Ammah’s brethren preach.
unspecified_visual_details: The location and appearance of the gathering.
The content of the contention.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent the words spoken in the contention.

title: The Missionaries Go to Middoni
summary: Seeing that the people would harden their hearts, the missionaries leave and go to Middoni. They preach to many there, but few believe.

explicit_facts.text: When they saw the people would harden their hearts, they departed and came to Middoni.
They preached to many in Middoni, and few believed their words.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The missionaries travel from Ani-Anti to Middoni and preach there.
unspecified_visual_details: The route and travel conditions.
The identity of the few who believed.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: The scene shows the move and their preaching in Middoni, not an invented specific speech.

title: Aaron and Others Imprisoned
summary: Aaron and a certain number of his brethren are taken and cast into prison; the rest flee from Middoni to the surrounding regions.

explicit_facts.text: Aaron and a certain number of his brethren were taken and cast into prison.
The remainder fled from Middoni to the surrounding regions.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Some missionaries are being taken to prison while others flee.
unspecified_visual_details: Who takes them, since the verse does not identify the captors.
The prison’s appearance and the exact number imprisoned or fleeing.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent the identity of the captors.

title: The Prisoners Are Delivered
summary: Those cast into prison suffer many things, then Lamoni and Ammon deliver them and provide food and clothing. The missionaries go forth again to declare the word.

explicit_facts.text: Those cast into prison suffered many things and were delivered by Lamoni and Ammon, who fed and clothed them.
They went forth again to declare the word after being delivered from prison for the first time.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Lamoni and Ammon helping the released prisoners with food and clothing.
unspecified_visual_details: The nature of the suffering.
The food, clothing, and prison’s appearance.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verses state they were delivered and provided for but do not describe the method of their release.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict specific injuries or forms of mistreatment.

title: Preaching in Synagogues and Assemblies
summary: The missionaries preach wherever they are led, in Amalekite synagogues or Lamanite assemblies where admitted. The Lord begins to bless them, and many come to the knowledge of truth and are convinced of their sins and incorrect traditions.

explicit_facts.text: The missionaries preached in every Amalekite synagogue or Lamanite assembly where they could be admitted.
The Lord began to bless them; they brought many to knowledge of the truth and convinced many of their sins and incorrect traditions.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Missionaries preaching to gathered listeners in different assemblies.
unspecified_visual_details: Which specific assemblies are shown.
How listeners visibly respond.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: The Lord’s blessing is reported, not described as a visible appearance.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Lord appearing or invent specific conversions.

title: Ammon and Lamoni Return to Ishmael
summary: Ammon and Lamoni return from Middoni to Ishmael, Lamoni’s land of inheritance. Lamoni does not allow Ammon to serve him or be his servant.

explicit_facts.text: Ammon and Lamoni returned from Middoni to Ishmael, the land of Lamoni’s inheritance.
King Lamoni would not suffer Ammon to serve him or be his servant.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Ammon and Lamoni traveling from Middoni to Ishmael.
unspecified_visual_details: Their route, travel means, and manner of arrival.
How Lamoni communicates his refusal.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: No direct dialogue is supplied for Lamoni’s refusal.

title: Lamoni Orders Synagogues Built
summary: Lamoni causes synagogues to be built in Ishmael and causes the people under his reign to assemble together.

explicit_facts.text: Lamoni caused synagogues to be built in Ishmael and caused his people to assemble.

reasonable_visual_inferences: People assembling at synagogues in Ishmael.
unspecified_visual_details: The synagogues’ design and construction materials.
The size and composition of the assembly.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a specific ceremony or speech.

title: Lamoni Teaches His People
summary: Lamoni rejoices over the people and teaches them. He declares that they are free from his father’s oppression and may worship the Lord according to their desires throughout the land under his reign.

explicit_facts.text: Lamoni rejoiced over the people and taught them many things.
He declared they were free from the oppression of his father, who had granted him rule over Ishmael and the surrounding land.
He declared they could worship the Lord according to their desires anywhere in the land under his reign.

unspecified_visual_details: The words of Lamoni’s teaching beyond the reported summary.
The setting and gestures of his address.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verses summarize Lamoni’s declarations rather than quote them directly.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Lamoni’s father as present.

title: Ammon Teaches Lamoni’s People
summary: Ammon preaches righteousness to Lamoni’s people and exhorts them daily. They heed his word and are zealous to keep God’s commandments.

explicit_facts.text: Ammon preached and taught Lamoni’s people about righteousness, exhorting them daily with diligence.
The people heeded Ammon’s word and were zealous to keep God’s commandments.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Ammon preaching to a gathered group of Lamoni’s people.
unspecified_visual_details: The specific teachings and the people’s visible expressions.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: The people’s response is summarized; no direct words are given.
